name: MCP CI

# auto-ontology-mcp is its own distribution with its own lightweight dependency set, so
# it gets its own workflow rather than riding along with the backend's: it needs
# no database drivers, no model tooling, and no NGC access, and installs in
# seconds.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'mcp/**'
      - '.github/workflows/ci-mcp.yml'

jobs:
  lint_and_format:
    name: Ruff Check & Format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Ruff lint
        uses: astral-sh/ruff-action@v4.1.0
        with:
          version: '0.15.9'
          args: check
          src: './mcp'

      - name: Ruff format check
        uses: astral-sh/ruff-action@v4.1.0
        with:
          version: '0.15.9'
          args: format --check
          src: './mcp'

  test:
    name: Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true

      # Installs the package itself, so the tests exercise the same import
      # path and packaged spec that a user's `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` would.
      - name: Sync dependencies
        working-directory: mcp
        run: uv sync

      - name: Pytest
        working-directory: mcp
        run: uv run pytest -q

  packaging:
    name: Wheel installs and runs standalone
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true

      # The failure this guards is specific: the server reads the OpenAPI spec
      # from disk, so a wheel that omits it builds and installs cleanly and then
      # dies at startup. Building and running outside the source tree is the
      # only way to catch that.
      - name: Build wheel
        working-directory: mcp
        run: uv build --wheel --out-dir dist

      - name: Install the wheel into a clean environment
        run: |
          uv venv /tmp/probe
          VIRTUAL_ENV=/tmp/probe uv pip install mcp/dist/*.whl

      - name: Server starts and lists its tools from outside the repo
        run: |
          cd /tmp
          /tmp/probe/bin/python - <<'PY'
          import asyncio
          from fastmcp import Client
          from auto_ontology_mcp.config import load_settings
          from auto_ontology_mcp.server import build_server
          from auto_ontology_mcp.tools import CURATED

          mcp, client = build_server(load_settings())

          # Derived rather than a literal count: the curated tools exist only if
          # the wheel carried the spec, which is what this job is guarding, and a
          # tool added or renamed upstream should not have to be restated here.
          expected = {spec.name for spec in CURATED} | {"ask_question", "check_readiness"}

          async def main() -> None:
              try:
                  async with Client(mcp) as session:
                      names = {t.name for t in await session.list_tools()}
                      icons = session.initialize_result.serverInfo.icons or []
              finally:
                  await client.aclose()
              assert names == expected, sorted(names ^ expected)
              # The icon is read from disk too, so it fails the same way.
              assert icons, "the wheel did not carry the icon"
              print(f"ok: {len(names)} tools and an icon from an installed wheel")

          asyncio.run(main())
          PY

name: OpenAPI CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'frontend/app/api/**'
      - 'frontend/scripts/generate-openapi.ts'
      # Also inputs to auto-ontology-api.json: the shared zod shapes are inlined into it,
      # the contract types shape what the declarations may express, and the
      # package version is written to `info.version`.
      - 'frontend/lib/openapiSchemas.ts'
      - 'frontend/types/openapi.ts'
      - 'frontend/package.json'
      - 'auto_ontology/**'
      - 'dev_tools/generate_backend_openapi.py'
      - 'docs/openapi/**'
      # The spec is committed here as well, so a hand-edit must be caught.
      - 'mcp/auto_ontology_mcp/auto-ontology-api.json'

jobs:
  # The public spec is generated from the route handlers plus the *committed*
  # backend spec, so this job needs Node only — no Python, no running server.
  public_spec:
    name: Public spec is up to date
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Install pnpm
        # Held at v4 for the reason ci-client.yml gives: the enterprise action
        # allowlist does not admit v5.
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: '10.33.0'
          run_install: false

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: frontend
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Regenerate
        working-directory: frontend
        run: pnpm openapi

      # `pnpm openapi` writes the packaged copy too (auto-ontology-mcp reads it at
      # startup and must work outside a checkout), so both paths are diffed.
      - name: Fail if the committed spec drifted
        run: |
          git diff --exit-code -- docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json mcp/auto_ontology_mcp/auto-ontology-api.json \
            || { echo '::error::the committed OpenAPI spec is stale — run `pnpm openapi` and commit both files'; exit 1; }

  # Building the FastAPI apps needs the full backend environment, so this job
  # is the expensive one; it only guards the internal spec it produces.
  backend_spec:
    name: Backend spec is up to date
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true

      - name: Sync dependencies
        run: uv sync --frozen

      - name: Regenerate
        run: uv run python -m dev_tools.generate_backend_openapi

      - name: Fail if the committed spec drifted
        run: |
          git diff --exit-code -- docs/openapi/backend.json docs/openapi/ingestion.json \
            || { echo '::error::docs/openapi/*.json is stale — run `uv run python -m dev_tools.generate_backend_openapi` and commit the result'; exit 1; }

# OpenAPI specs

Generated files — do not edit by hand. Each is committed so it can be reviewed
in a pull request diff and consumed without a running server; CI regenerates
them and fails if what you committed is stale.

| File                                 | Describes                               | Generated by                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| [`auto-ontology-api.json`](./auto-ontology-api.json)     | **The public API.**                     | `pnpm openapi` (from `frontend/`)                     |
| [`backend.json`](./backend.json)     | Internal Auto Ontology FastAPI app.               | `uv run python -m dev_tools.generate_backend_openapi` |
| [`ingestion.json`](./ingestion.json) | Internal Ingestion Service FastAPI app. | same as above                                         |

## Which one do consumers want?

`auto-ontology-api.json`. The Python services are ClusterIP-only and reachable solely
through the Next.js proxy, so `backend.json` and `ingestion.json` describe an
internal surface nobody outside the cluster can call. They exist because
`auto-ontology-api.json` is built partly from them.

`auto-ontology-api.json` also carries things the FastAPI specs cannot know:

- `x-auto-ontology-permissions` — the permission a caller needs, read from each route's
  `withPermission({...})` wrapper (or `"public"` for `withPublic`), plus the
  401/403 responses that implies. The same wrapper decides each operation's
  `security`: the `ApiToken` scheme, or `[]` for a `withPublic` route.
- `x-auto-ontology-source` — the `route.ts` that serves the operation.
- `x-auto-ontology-proxied` — whether the handler forwards to FastAPI or answers itself.
- `x-auto-ontology-upstream` — for the chat routes, the backend path whose response is
  relayed.

## How it is built

`frontend/scripts/generate-openapi.ts` walks `frontend/app/api/**/route.ts` with
ts-morph — file-based routing makes the paths deterministic — and fills in
schemas from two sources:

- **Proxied handlers** (`proxyToBackend`) forward the pathname verbatim, so
  their schemas are merged from `backend.json` by matching path and method.
- **Everything else** — the Prisma-backed handlers, which have no FastAPI
  counterpart, and the chat handlers, which build their own upstream request —
  declares its shapes in a sibling `app/api/**/openapi.ts` module using zod.
  See `frontend/types/openapi.ts` for that contract. The declaration lives
  beside `route.ts` rather than inside it because a plain Node script cannot
  import a route handler (`next/headers`, `after()`, `getPrisma()`).

Only the component schemas the public spec actually references are copied over,
closed transitively.

## Regenerating

```sh
uv run python -m dev_tools.generate_backend_openapi   # backend.json, ingestion.json
cd frontend && pnpm openapi                           # auto-ontology-api.json
```

Run them in that order — the public spec reads the committed `backend.json`.

## Viewing

The spec is deployed to Github Page in the following line: <https://friendly-adventure-38857y4.pages.github.io/>
Later will be part of Auto Ontology Docs on Nvidia website

Or paste the file into <https://docs.scalar.com/swagger-editor> — bearing in
mind that hands the full API surface to a third party.

## Conventions

**The API is snake_case throughout** — path segments, path and query
parameters, request bodies and response fields. A new endpoint is expected to
follow that, whatever the naming of the code behind it:

- Dynamic route folders are named for the parameter they carry, in snake_case:
  `app/api/terms/[term_id]/route.ts` → `/api/terms/{term_id}`.
- The Prisma models behind the frontend-only routes use snake_case field names,
  so a row serialises straight to the API shape with no mapping layer.
- Where the code behind a route is camelCase and cannot change, the handler
  maps at the boundary rather than leaking it: the Better Auth models (`User`,
  `Session`, `Account`, `SsoProvider`) are generated camelCase, and
  `GET /api/sso-providers` publishes `provider_id`. `GET /api/sso-discovery`
  likewise relays the OpenID Connect Discovery document under its own
  standard names.
- Internal TypeScript keeps normal camelCase locals and UI types; only what
  crosses the wire is snake_case.

The generator enforces some of this: it refuses to publish a route whose
`withPermission(...)` argument it cannot read, and fails on any `route.ts`
that exports no HTTP method it recognises, so nothing is dropped silently.

## Known limitations

- No `servers` block yet: the spec says how to authenticate, but not against
  which host.
- Most schemas carry `additionalProperties: true`. Backend response models are
  deliberately permissive — FastAPI _drops_ undeclared fields when a
  `response_model` is set, so a strict model would silently break responses
  rather than merely document them. Listed fields are reliable; the list is not
  guaranteed exhaustive.
- `PATCH /api/nodes/{node_id}` returns `NodeUpdateResult | null`, whose fields
  are all optional: the body echoes only the properties the request patched.
  The route also accepts any of them for any node type — `sample_values` is
  meaningful on a Column but is not rejected on a Database.
- `/api/auth/{all}` is Better Auth's catch-all. It appears in the spec, but its
  per-endpoint request and response shapes are the library's and are not
  mirrored here.

# Renders docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json as a Redoc site and publishes it to GitHub
# Pages, because GitHub itself has no OpenAPI viewer — the committed JSON is
# readable by tooling, not by people.
#
# BEFORE THIS CAN RUN: Settings → Pages → Source must be set to "GitHub
# Actions". Until then this job fails; the deploy step is what needs it.
#
# ON VISIBILITY: this repository is private, but a Pages site is only private
# on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with private Pages enabled. Anywhere else the
# published site — the whole API surface, including which permission each
# operation requires — is world-readable. Confirm the Pages visibility setting
# before merging.

name: Publish API docs

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json"
      - ".github/workflows/publish-api-docs.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Never let two publishes race; drop queued runs rather than deploying stale
# docs, but let an in-flight one finish so Pages is not left half-updated.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    name: Build and deploy Redoc
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      - name: Build the Redoc site
        env:
          REDOCLY_TELEMETRY: off
        # Pinned to v1: `build-docs` was removed in v2.
        run: npx --yes @redocly/cli@1 build-docs docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json -o site/index.html

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: site

      - name: Deploy
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

# Builds the Auto Ontology MCP server image and pushes it to nvcr.io. The Astra deploy
# repo consumes it by digest. Requires repo secret:
#   NGC_API_KEY - an NGC API key with push access to nvcr.io/nvstaging/gsf

name: 'Staging: Publish MCP image to nvcr.io'

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Override image tag (default: stg.<timestamp>)'
        required: false
  push:
    branches: [main, feat/astra-nightly-deploy]
    paths:
      - 'mcp/**'
      - '.github/workflows/staging-publish-mcp.yml'

env:
  IMAGE: nvcr.io/nvstaging/gsf/auto-ontology-mcp

jobs:
  publish-mcp:
    name: Build & push amd64 MCP image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Compute image tag
        id: meta
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          t='${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}'
          if [ -z "$t" ]; then
            t="stg.$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
          fi
          echo "tag=$t" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Image tag: $t"

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

      - name: Login to nvcr.io
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: nvcr.io
          username: '$oauthtoken'
          password: ${{ secrets.NGC_API_KEY }}

      - name: Build & push (linux/amd64)
        id: build
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: ./mcp
          file: mcp/Dockerfile
          platforms: linux/amd64
          push: true
          tags: ${{ env.IMAGE }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}
          provenance: false

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          {
            echo "### Published MCP image"
            echo ""
            echo "- Image: \`${IMAGE}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}\`"
            echo "- Digest: \`${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}\`"
            echo ""
            echo "Pin in the umbrella as:"
            echo '```yaml'
            echo "mcp:"
            echo "  image:"
            echo "    repository: ${IMAGE}"
            echo "    tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}"
            echo "    digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}"
            echo '```'
          } >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# Publishes the Auto Ontology Helm chart to the NGC Helm chart registry as
# <org>[/<team>]/<chart-name>:<version>. Run release-docker.yml first.
#
# The chart is staged in nvstaging/gsf but names the images' published paths
# (<image-registry>, default nvcr.io/nvidia): NGC Catalog publishing copies
# it to nvidia unmodified, and customers cannot pull from nvstaging.
# dev_tools/release_helm_chart.py refuses to publish unless values.yaml names
# exactly <image-registry>/<image>:<app-version>.
#
# Run it on a release branch: dispatched on release/v1.0 with no versions, it
# packages that branch as chart 1.0.0 deploying images tagged 1.0.
# Requires repo secret:
#   NGC_API_KEY - an NGC API key with chart write access to <org>[/<team>]
#                 (shared with the staging-publish-* workflows, so the key
#                 must also keep push access to nvcr.io/nvstaging/gsf)

name: Release - Helm Chart

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Chart version, SemVer (e.g. 1.0.0); empty for the app version padded to SemVer'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      app-version:
        description: 'Image tag the chart deploys (e.g. 1.0); empty to take it from the release/vX.Y branch'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      source-ref:
        description: 'Git ref to build from; empty for the branch this runs on'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      org:
        description: 'NGC org'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'nvstaging'
      team:
        description: 'NGC team (empty for org level)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'gsf'
      image-registry:
        description: 'Registry values.yaml must name: where the images are once published'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'nvcr.io/nvidia'
      dry-run:
        description: 'Build chart without publishing to NGC'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      chart-name:
        description: 'Helm chart name'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'auto-ontology'

  # Called by release-all.yml, with the same inputs as a manual run.
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Chart version, SemVer (e.g. 1.0.0); empty for the app version padded to SemVer'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      app-version:
        description: 'Image tag the chart deploys (e.g. 1.0); empty to take it from the release/vX.Y branch'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      source-ref:
        description: 'Git ref to build from; empty for the branch this runs on'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      org:
        description: 'NGC org'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'nvstaging'
      team:
        description: 'NGC team (empty for org level)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'gsf'
      image-registry:
        description: 'Registry values.yaml must name: where the images are once published'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'nvcr.io/nvidia'
      dry-run:
        description: 'Build chart without publishing to NGC'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      chart-name:
        description: 'Helm chart name'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'auto-ontology'
    secrets:
      NGC_API_KEY:
        required: true

env:
  HELM_CHART_DIR: helm/auto-ontology

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  determine-version:
    name: Determine Release Version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      app-version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      chart-version: ${{ inputs.version || steps.version.outputs.chart-version }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5.1.0
        with:
          sparse-checkout: .github/actions
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Extract version from branch or input
        id: version
        uses: ./.github/actions/determine-release-version
        with:
          version: ${{ inputs.app-version }}

  release-helm:
    name: Build & Publish Helm Chart
    needs: determine-version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      CHART_VERSION: ${{ needs.determine-version.outputs.chart-version }}
      APP_VERSION: ${{ needs.determine-version.outputs.app-version }}
      NGC_CLI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.NGC_API_KEY }}
      NGC_CLI_ORG: ${{ inputs.org }}
      NGC_CLI_TEAM: ${{ inputs.team }}
      NGC_CLI_FORMAT_TYPE: json
      # Dispatch inputs reach the shell through the environment, never by
      # interpolation into a script that runs with the NGC key available.
      ORG: ${{ inputs.org }}
      TEAM: ${{ inputs.team }}
      CHART_NAME: ${{ inputs.chart-name }}
      IMAGE_REGISTRY: ${{ inputs.image-registry }}
      DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry-run }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@fbc6f3992d24b796d5a048ff273f7fcc4a7b6c09 # v5.1.0
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.source-ref || github.ref }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Helm
        uses: azure/setup-helm@9bc31f4ebc9c6b171d7bfbaa5d006ae7abdb4310 # v5.0.1

      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@ece7cb06caefa5fff74198d8649806c4678c61a1 # v6.3.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: pip install ngcsdk pyyaml

      - name: Lint Helm chart
        run: helm lint "${HELM_CHART_DIR}"

      - name: Release Helm chart
        run: |
          DRY_RUN_FLAG=""
          if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "true" ]; then
            DRY_RUN_FLAG="--dry-run"
          fi
          python dev_tools/release_helm_chart.py \
            --org "$ORG" \
            --team "$TEAM" \
            --name "$CHART_NAME" \
            --chart-dir "${HELM_CHART_DIR}" \
            --version "${CHART_VERSION}" \
            --app-version "${APP_VERSION}" \
            --image-registry "$IMAGE_REGISTRY" \
            $DRY_RUN_FLAG

      - name: Upload packaged chart artifact
        if: ${{ inputs.dry-run }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f # v6.0.0
        with:
          name: auto-ontology-helm-chart
          path: dist/${{ inputs.chart-name }}-${{ env.CHART_VERSION }}.tgz
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "### Helm Chart Release" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| Setting | Value |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "|---------|-------|" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| Chart source | \`${HELM_CHART_DIR}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| Chart | \`$CHART_NAME\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| Version | \`${CHART_VERSION}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| App version (image tag) | \`${APP_VERSION}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| Images (as published) | \`${IMAGE_REGISTRY}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| NGC | \`${ORG}${TEAM:+/$TEAM}/${CHART_NAME}:${CHART_VERSION}\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| Dry Run | \`$DRY_RUN\` |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: Auto Ontology CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      # Not just `auto_ontology/**`: the fixtures, the migrations and the lockfile all
      # change what the suite does, and a green run that skipped them because
      # only `alembic/` changed would be worthless.
      - 'auto_ontology/**'
      - 'dev_tools/**'
      - 'alembic/**'
      - 'pyproject.toml'
      - 'uv.lock'
      - '.github/workflows/ci-python.yml'

jobs:
  lint_and_format:
    name: Ruff Check & Format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      # Every directory holding Python, not just `auto_ontology/`. The migrations and the
      # fixture tooling are as easy to break as anything else, and they were
      # unchecked here while passing locally — so the first thing to land badly
      # formatted would have been the thing nobody ran ruff over.
      - name: Ruff lint
        uses: astral-sh/ruff-action@v4.1.0
        with:
          version: '0.16.5'
          args: check
          src: './auto_ontology ./alembic ./dev_tools'

      - name: Ruff format check
        uses: astral-sh/ruff-action@v4.1.0
        with:
          version: '0.16.5'
          args: format --check
          src: './auto_ontology ./alembic ./dev_tools'

  build_image:
    name: Build Auto Ontology Server image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The `secrets` context is not allowed in `if:` expressions, so surface the
    # NGC key as an env var and gate the nvcr.io login on that instead. The
    # Dockerfile FROMs nvcr.io/nvidia/base/ubuntu; in-org PRs pull it
    # authenticated, forks fall back to an anonymous pull.
    env:
      NGC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.NGC_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android /usr/share/dotnet /opt/ghc \
            /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL /usr/local/share/boost || true
          df -h /

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

      - name: Login to nvcr.io (for base image)
        if: ${{ env.NGC_API_KEY != '' }}
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: nvcr.io
          username: '$oauthtoken'
          password: ${{ env.NGC_API_KEY }}

      - name: Build Auto Ontology Server image (no push)
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: .
          file: Dockerfile
          platforms: linux/amd64
          push: false
          load: false
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=server
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=server
          provenance: false

  tests:
    name: Pytest (with Postgres fixtures)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # pgvector, not plain postgres: the vector store creates its collections
    # with `CREATE EXTENSION vector`, and `stock postgres` fails there in a way
    # that looks like a Auto Ontology bug. Pinned to the same tag as docker-compose.yml so
    # CI and a developer's laptop disagree about nothing.
    services:
      postgres:
        image: pgvector/pgvector:pg17
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: auto_ontology
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: auto_ontology
          POSTGRES_DB: auto_ontology
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U auto_ontology -d auto_ontology"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 20

    env:
      POSTGRES_HOST: localhost
      POSTGRES_PORT: '5432'
      POSTGRES_USER: auto_ontology
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: auto_ontology
      POSTGRES_DATABASE: auto_ontology

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: uv.lock

      # `--extra kumo` so the real-SDK Kumo tests run rather than skip. The
      # wheels are vendored in `vendor/wheels` (flat index, cp312 manylinux
      # x86_64 included) and every other dependency of kumorfm is already in
      # the base tree, so this costs a few seconds and needs no index access.
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --locked --extra kumo

      # Everything below is the documented local setup from
      # dev_tools/fixtures/sql/README.md, in the same order. No credentials:
      # the fixture SQL is committed, and the graph fixture is hand-authored with embedding
      # stubbed out precisely so it needs no LLM or embedding endpoint.
      - name: Seed the fixture databases (pagila, chinook)
        run: uv run --no-sync python -m dev_tools.fixtures.seed_fixtures

      - name: Migrate the Auto Ontology schema
        run: uv run --no-sync alembic upgrade head

      - name: Seed the deterministic graph fixture
        env:
          CONNECTION_STRINGS: >-
            postgresql://auto_ontology:auto_ontology@localhost:5432/pagila,sqlite:///${{ github.workspace }}/dev_tools/fixtures/sql/chinook.sqlite
        run: uv run --no-sync python -m dev_tools.fixtures.seed_graph_fixture --reset

      # `make migrate-check` — the migrations must describe the models. Placed
      # after the upgrade because `alembic check` compares a live database
      # against auto_ontology/dal/schema.py, so it needs one at the head revision. Catches
      # a model edited without a matching revision, which otherwise surfaces as
      # an UndefinedColumn in whichever environment deploys first.
      - name: Fail if the schema has drifted from the models
        run: uv run --no-sync alembic check

      # `-p no:randomly` is not set and no `-x`: the point of this job is the
      # whole picture, including how many of the fixture-backed tests ran.
      - name: Run the test suite
        run: uv run --no-sync pytest auto_ontology dev_tools -q --durations=10

      # A skip guard naming the wrong dependency turns a suite off silently and
      # still reports green -- which is how the golden replay and the live
      # connector tests sat unrun. Only the two live-warehouse tests
      # (AUTO_ONTOLOGY_LIVE_DATABRICKS / AUTO_ONTOLOGY_LIVE_MYSQL) may skip here.
      - name: Fail if the fixture-backed tests silently skipped
        run: |
          skipped=$(uv run --no-sync pytest auto_ontology dev_tools -q -rs 2>/dev/null \
            | grep -c '^SKIPPED' || true)
          echo "skipped: $skipped"
          if [ "$skipped" -gt 2 ]; then
            echo "::error::$skipped tests skipped; expected at most 2 (live" \
                 "Databricks and MySQL). A fixture is probably unreachable, so" \
                 "this run proved less than it appears to."
            uv run --no-sync pytest auto_ontology dev_tools -q -rs 2>/dev/null \
              | grep '^SKIPPED' || true
            exit 1
          fi

on:

    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'frontend/**'

defaults:
  run:
    working-directory: frontend

jobs:
  lint_and_build:
    name: Prettier, ESLint & Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Install pnpm
        # Held at v4: the enterprise action allowlist does not admit v5, and a
        # blocked action fails the workflow before any step runs. The Node 20
        # deprecation warning it emits is the lesser cost.
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: '10.33.0'
          run_install: false

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - name: Get pnpm store directory
        shell: bash
        run: echo "STORE_PATH=$(pnpm store path --silent)" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Setup pnpm cache
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ env.STORE_PATH }}
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-store-${{ hashFiles('frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pnpm-store-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Prettier check
        run: pnpm format:check

      - name: ESLint
        run: pnpm lint

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm build

  build_image:
    name: Build frontend image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Override the workflow-level `working-directory: frontend`: this job's first
    # `run:` step (Free disk space) executes before checkout, when `frontend/`
    # does not exist yet. `uses:` actions ignore this anyway, so the
    # build-push-action `context: ./frontend` still resolves from the repo root.
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: .
    # The `secrets` context is not allowed in `if:` expressions, so surface the
    # NGC key as an env var and gate the nvcr.io login on that instead.
    env:
      NGC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.NGC_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android /usr/share/dotnet /opt/ghc \
            /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL /usr/local/share/boost || true
          df -h /

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

      - name: Login to nvcr.io (for base image)
        if: ${{ env.NGC_API_KEY != '' }}
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: nvcr.io
          username: '$oauthtoken'
          password: ${{ env.NGC_API_KEY }}

      - name: Build frontend image (no push)
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: ./frontend
          file: frontend/Dockerfile
          platforms: linux/amd64
          push: false
          load: false
          build-args: |
            PYTHON_API_URL=http://auto-ontology:3001
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=frontend
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=frontend
          provenance: false

# Deliberately a separate distribution from `auto-ontology-server`, not an extra on it.
# The MCP server reaches Auto Ontology over HTTP like any other client, so it needs none
# of the backend's database drivers or model tooling — installing
# `auto-ontology-server` to run it would pull ~450 packages and over a gigabyte, and it
# would inherit that project's git dependencies. These four deps install in
# seconds, which is what makes `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` practical on a laptop.

[project]
name = "auto-ontology-mcp"
version = "1.1.0"
description = "MCP server exposing the Auto Ontology semantic layer to agent harnesses"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }
dependencies = [
    "fastmcp>=3.2.4,<4",
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    "pydantic>=2",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0",
]

[project.scripts]
auto-ontology-mcp = "auto_ontology_mcp.__main__:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["auto_ontology_mcp"]

# The tool surface is generated from this spec at startup, so it has to travel
# with the package. Kept in sync with docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json by
# `pnpm openapi`, which writes both copies, and enforced by CI.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"auto_ontology_mcp/auto-ontology-api.json" = "auto_ontology_mcp/auto-ontology-api.json"
"auto_ontology_mcp/nvidia-mark.svg" = "auto_ontology_mcp/nvidia-mark.svg"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]

[dependency-groups]
dev = ["pytest>=8"]

[tool.uv]
# Patched version of a transitive dependency flagged by nSpect.
constraint-dependencies = [
    "pyjwt>=2.15.1",  # BDSA-2026-35552 (via mcp)
]

"""Sign-in, where Auto Ontology itself is the authorization server.

This server could instead sit between the client and the deployment's identity
provider. That works, but it has to be told a client id, a client secret, and a
redirect URI that someone registered with that provider first — a ticket for
every deployment, and a secret to hold and rotate. Auto Ontology already knows how to sign
a person in, including through SSO, so it does, and this server carries no
credentials at all.

What that buys, concretely:

* Nothing to configure beyond pointing at Auto Ontology. Clients register themselves
  through dynamic client registration, which Auto Ontology supports and most corporate
  providers do not, so no redirect URI is ever registered by hand.
* No secret on disk here, and no secret to rotate.
* The registrations and grants live in Auto Ontology's database, so replicas share them
  and a restart does not sign anyone out.
* Revocation is Auto Ontology's: deleting the grant, banning the user, or changing their
  role takes effect on the next call.

The token a caller presents is one Auto Ontology minted, so verifying it is a question
only Auto Ontology can answer — hence the round trip below. There is no local signature to
check: these tokens are opaque by design, which also means they leak nothing if
logged. The same token is then forwarded upstream unchanged, where
``frontend/auth/resolve-user.ts`` resolves it to its owner.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import httpx
from fastmcp.server.auth.auth import AccessToken, RemoteAuthProvider, TokenVerifier
from fastmcp.utilities.logging import get_logger
from pydantic import AnyHttpUrl

from auto_ontology_mcp.config import Settings

logger = get_logger(__name__)

# Better Auth 1.7's OAuth Provider validates a bearer at UserInfo without
# requiring this resource server to hold client credentials. Auto Ontology adds the
# issuing client and granted scope as private claims for FastMCP's AccessToken.
USERINFO_PATH = "/api/auth/oauth2/userinfo"
CLIENT_ID_CLAIM = "urn:auto-ontology:oauth:client_id"
SCOPE_CLAIM = "urn:auto-ontology:oauth:scope"


class AutoOntologyTokenVerifier(TokenVerifier):
    """Validates a token by asking Auto Ontology whether it still stands.

    A rejected token returns ``None`` so the caller is told to sign in again.
    A Auto Ontology that cannot be reached raises instead: an outage is not an expired
    token, and answering "unauthenticated" would send everyone through a
    sign-in that cannot succeed either.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        api_url: str,
        timeout_s: float,
        transport: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self._api_url = api_url
        self._timeout_s = timeout_s
        # A short-lived client of its own rather than the one the tools share:
        # that one rewrites the Authorization header to the caller's credential,
        # which is the very thing being checked here. `transport` is a seam for
        # tests.
        self._transport = transport

    async def verify_token(self, token: str) -> AccessToken | None:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(
            base_url=self._api_url,
            timeout=self._timeout_s,
            transport=self._transport,
        ) as client:
            response = await client.get(
                USERINFO_PATH, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
            )

        if response.status_code >= 500:
            response.raise_for_status()

        # Unknown, expired, or revoked tokens receive a 4xx response. Anything
        # unparseable is treated the same way: a body we cannot read is not an
        # identity, and raising here would turn a refusal into a server error.
        try:
            user_info = response.json() if response.status_code == 200 else None
        except ValueError:
            user_info = None

        if not isinstance(user_info, dict) or not user_info.get("sub"):
            logger.debug("Auto Ontology rejected an access token")
            return None

        # Space-separated per RFC 6749, and absent when the grant carries none.
        scopes = str(user_info.get(SCOPE_CLAIM) or "").split()

        return AccessToken(
            token=token,
            # The client that was granted the token, which FastMCP uses to
            # attribute the session. Registration guarantees it.
            client_id=str(user_info.get(CLIENT_ID_CLAIM) or "unknown"),
            scopes=scopes,
            subject=str(user_info["sub"]),
        )


def build_auto_ontology_auth(settings: Settings) -> RemoteAuthProvider:
    """Advertise Auto Ontology as the authorization server for this MCP server.

    Publishing Auto Ontology's URL here is the whole handshake: a client that gets a 401
    reads this server's protected-resource metadata, finds Auto Ontology, discovers Auto Ontology's
    endpoints, registers itself, and sends the user to Auto Ontology's ordinary login
    page — which already knows how to do SSO.
    """
    return RemoteAuthProvider(
        token_verifier=AutoOntologyTokenVerifier(
            settings.api_url, timeout_s=settings.timeout_s
        ),
        authorization_servers=[AnyHttpUrl(settings.api_url)],
        base_url=settings.public_url,
        resource_name="Auto Ontology",
    )


def auto_ontology_access_token() -> str | None:
    """The token this request was authenticated with, to forward to Auto Ontology.

    Read back from FastMCP rather than off the incoming header so that what is
    forwarded is the token that actually passed verification.
    """

    # Imported here because it resolves request state: at module scope it would
    # bind at import time, outside any request.
    from fastmcp.server.dependencies import get_access_token

    try:
        token = get_access_token()
    except Exception:
        # Raised when there is no authenticated request in scope, which is a
        # normal state rather than a fault.
        return None

    return getattr(token, "token", None) or None


__all__ = [
    "CLIENT_ID_CLAIM",
    "AutoOntologyTokenVerifier",
    "SCOPE_CLAIM",
    "USERINFO_PATH",
    "build_auto_ontology_auth",
    "auto_ontology_access_token",
]

# auto-ontology-mcp

An [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for
[Auto Ontology](https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology). It lets any
MCP-capable agent — Cursor, Claude Desktop, an internal agent — ask questions in
natural language about the data a Auto Ontology deployment is connected to, and inspect the
semantic layer behind the answers.

## Install and run

`uvx` fetches, builds, and runs it straight from the repository, so there is
nothing to clone:

```sh
uvx --from "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git#subdirectory=mcp" auto-ontology-mcp
```

From a checkout of this directory, `uvx --from . auto-ontology-mcp` does the same.

> [!NOTE]
> Auto Ontology is NVIDIA-internal today, so this install needs GitHub credentials with
> access to the repository. It becomes a plain `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` once the package is
> published to PyPI.

Run one server; people log in through it. The URL of your Auto Ontology deployment is the
only thing it needs to be told:

```sh
AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_URL=https://auto_ontology.example.com auto-ontology-mcp
```

## Connect a client

In Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`) or Claude Desktop
(`claude_desktop_config.json`), point at the URL. There are no credentials in the
config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "auto-ontology": {
      "url": "https://auto-ontology-mcp.example/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

The client offers to sign in, the user gets Auto Ontology's normal login page, and every
call afterwards runs as that person.

Then ask something like *"what does Auto Ontology mean by an active customer, and how many
were there last quarter?"*

## Tools

`ask_question` is the one that answers questions: it runs Auto Ontology's text-to-SQL agent
and returns the answer, the SQL it ran, and the rows. The rest — `search_terms`,
`describe_table`, `check_answerable` and friends — let an agent learn the
vocabulary and check its assumptions first.

Every tool reads, and every tool works through the semantic layer: there is none
for browsing databases, schemas, or raw columns. Nothing here modifies the
glossary, the catalog, or the underlying databases.

## Notes

This server is a plain HTTP client of the Auto Ontology API, so it needs no database
credentials and can run anywhere that can reach your deployment. It holds no
credentials of its own either — Auto Ontology signs each caller in — so it never has more
access than the person calling it.

Full documentation — all configuration variables, the complete tool list, and how
to extend it — is in [`docs/mcp.md`](../docs/mcp.md).

from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import pytest

from auto_ontology.retrieval.entity_coverage.agents import question_extraction
from auto_ontology.retrieval.entity_coverage.agents.question_extraction import (
    QuestionExtractionAgent,
)
from auto_ontology.retrieval.entity_coverage.models import QuestionExtractionLiteModel
from auto_ontology.retrieval.entity_coverage.prompts import (
    create_question_extraction_prompt,
)
from auto_ontology.retrieval.text_to_sql.agents import question_intent
from auto_ontology.retrieval.text_to_sql.agents.question_intent import (
    CalculationSubtype,
    QuestionIntentAgent,
    QuestionIntentModel,
    QuestionType,
)


def test_prompt_limits_evidence_to_sanitized_question_disambiguation() -> None:
    prompt = create_question_extraction_prompt(
        "Show points earned by customers",
        evidence="Points earned refers to loyalty_points, not reward_balance.",
        include_subject=False,
    )

    assert "## Evidence for sanitization" in prompt
    assert "at most one concise disambiguating qualifier" in prompt
    assert "Do not append or summarize the evidence" in prompt
    assert "derive entities only from the completed sanitized question" in prompt
    assert "Points earned refers to loyalty_points" in prompt
    assert "AVAILABLE TABLES" not in prompt


@pytest.mark.parametrize("evidence", [None, ""])
def test_prompt_omits_evidence_section_when_not_provided(
    evidence: str | None,
) -> None:
    prompt = create_question_extraction_prompt(
        "Show points earned by customers",
        evidence=evidence,
        include_subject=False,
    )

    assert "## Evidence for sanitization" not in prompt


def test_agent_forwards_state_evidence_without_changing_original_question(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    captured_messages: list = []

    def fake_invoke(
        _llm: object,
        messages: list,
        _schema: object,
    ) -> QuestionExtractionLiteModel:
        captured_messages.extend(messages)
        return QuestionExtractionLiteModel(
            sanitized_question="Show loyalty points earned by customers",
            required_entity_name=["loyalty points", "customer"],
        )

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        question_extraction,
        "invoke_with_structured_output",
        fake_invoke,
    )
    state = {
        "llm": MagicMock(),
        "initial_question": "Show points earned by customers",
        "evidence": "Points earned refers to loyalty_points.",
        "path_state": {},
        "glossary": [],
    }

    result = QuestionExtractionAgent(include_subject=False).execute(state)

    assert "Points earned refers to loyalty_points." in captured_messages[0].content
    assert state["initial_question"] == "Show points earned by customers"
    assert result["path_state"]["normalized_question"] == (
        "Show loyalty points earned by customers"
    )
    assert result["path_state"]["entities"] == ["loyalty points", "customer"]


def test_intent_rewrite_and_evidence_feed_question_extraction(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        question_intent,
        "invoke_with_structured_output",
        lambda *_args, **_kwargs: QuestionIntentModel(
            question_type=QuestionType.CALCULATION,
            calculation_subtype=CalculationSubtype.AGGREGATION,
            rewritten_question="find revenue",
            extracted_evidence="",
            target_db="test_dataset",
        ),
    )
    state = {
        "llm": MagicMock(),
        "initial_question": "find revenue in test_dataset dataset",
        "evidence": "Revenue means gross_sales minus refunds.",
        "path_state": {},
        "glossary": [],
        "connectors": [SimpleNamespace(database_name="test_dataset")],
    }
    state.update(QuestionIntentAgent().execute(state))
    captured_messages: list = []

    def fake_extract(
        _llm: object,
        messages: list,
        _schema: object,
    ) -> QuestionExtractionLiteModel:
        captured_messages.extend(messages)
        return QuestionExtractionLiteModel(
            sanitized_question="find revenue",
            required_entity_name=["revenue"],
        )

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        question_extraction,
        "invoke_with_structured_output",
        fake_extract,
    )

    result = QuestionExtractionAgent(include_subject=False).execute(state)

    prompt = captured_messages[0].content
    assert "## Input\n\nfind revenue" in prompt
    assert "Revenue means gross_sales minus refunds." in prompt
    assert "Use the test_dataset dataset." not in prompt
    assert state["path_state"]["target_db"] == "test_dataset"
    assert state["initial_question"] == "find revenue in test_dataset dataset"
    assert result["path_state"]["normalized_question"] == "find revenue"

"""The package carries what it needs to run outside a source checkout."""

from __future__ import annotations

import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

import auto_ontology_mcp
from auto_ontology_mcp.config import DEFAULT_SPEC_PATH
from auto_ontology_mcp.server import ICON_PATH

_PACKAGE_DIR = Path(auto_ontology_mcp.__file__).resolve().parent
_PROJECT_DIR = _PACKAGE_DIR.parent
_CANONICAL_SPEC = _PROJECT_DIR.parent / "docs" / "openapi" / "auto-ontology-api.json"
_CANONICAL_MARK = _PROJECT_DIR.parent / "frontend" / "public" / "favicon.svg"


def _pyproject() -> dict:
    return tomllib.loads((_PROJECT_DIR / "pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def test_spec_ships_inside_the_package() -> None:
    # Resolving it relative to the repo instead is what limited this to a
    # source checkout: an installed package has no docs/ directory above it.
    assert DEFAULT_SPEC_PATH.is_file()
    assert DEFAULT_SPEC_PATH.parent == _PACKAGE_DIR


def test_packaged_spec_matches_the_canonical_one() -> None:
    # `pnpm openapi` writes both copies; this fails if only one was committed.
    if not _CANONICAL_SPEC.is_file():
        pytest.skip("installed outside the repo; nothing to compare against")

    assert DEFAULT_SPEC_PATH.read_bytes() == _CANONICAL_SPEC.read_bytes(), (
        "The packaged spec drifted from docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json. "
        "Run `pnpm openapi` and commit both files."
    )


def test_icon_ships_inside_the_package() -> None:
    assert ICON_PATH.is_file()
    assert ICON_PATH.parent == _PACKAGE_DIR


def test_icon_matches_the_frontend_favicon() -> None:
    # Same mark the product shows, so the two cannot drift into different logos.
    if not _CANONICAL_MARK.is_file():
        pytest.skip("installed outside the repo; nothing to compare against")

    assert ICON_PATH.read_bytes() == _CANONICAL_MARK.read_bytes(), (
        "The packaged icon drifted from frontend/public/favicon.svg."
    )


def test_both_assets_are_forced_into_the_wheel() -> None:
    # Neither is a .py file, so hatchling only carries them if named here. The
    # failure is nasty: the wheel builds and installs, then reads from disk at
    # startup and finds nothing.
    forced = _pyproject()["tool"]["hatch"]["build"]["targets"]["wheel"]["force-include"]

    assert "auto_ontology_mcp/auto-ontology-api.json" in forced
    assert "auto_ontology_mcp/nvidia-mark.svg" in forced


def test_console_script_is_declared() -> None:
    # The whole point of the separate distribution: `auto-ontology-mcp` on PATH, and
    # `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` without installing anything.
    assert _pyproject()["project"]["scripts"] == {
        "auto-ontology-mcp": "auto_ontology_mcp.__main__:main"
    }


def test_stays_independent_of_the_backend_distribution() -> None:
    # Depending on auto-ontology-server would drag in ~450 packages and its git
    # dependencies, which is the thing this package exists to avoid.
    names = _pyproject()["project"]["dependencies"]

    assert not any("auto-ontology-server" in name for name in names)
    assert len(names) <= 5


def test_version_is_reported_not_raised() -> None:
    # Running from an uninstalled source tree is a normal way to develop and
    # must not stop the server from starting.
    assert isinstance(auto_ontology_mcp.get_version(), str)
    assert auto_ontology_mcp.get_version()

"""The curated allow-list stays honest about the API it claims to expose."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from types import SimpleNamespace

from auto_ontology_mcp.config import DEFAULT_SPEC_PATH
from auto_ontology_mcp.tools import (
    CURATED,
    apply_description,
    missing_from_spec,
    names_by_operation_id,
    route_maps,
)

SPEC = json.loads(DEFAULT_SPEC_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

# Anything that changes state. A read-only server is the whole safety argument
# for handing this to an autonomous agent, so it is asserted rather than assumed.
_WRITE_METHODS = {"POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"}

# The one exception: coverage grading is a POST because it takes a question in
# the body, but it only reads the semantic layer.
_READ_ONLY_POSTS = {"/api/question-entity-coverage"}


def test_every_curated_operation_exists_in_the_spec() -> None:
    # The guard that matters most: a renamed or removed endpoint would
    # otherwise silently drop its tool, leaving a server that starts fine but
    # is quietly missing capability.
    assert missing_from_spec(SPEC) == []


def test_nothing_walks_the_physical_catalog() -> None:
    # Consumers are meant to reach the data through the semantic layer. A tool
    # that lists databases, schemas, or raw columns invites an agent to reason
    # about tables directly instead, so these routes stay unpublished even
    # though the API offers them.
    physical = (
        "/api/datasources/dbs",
        "/api/schemas/",
        "/api/tables/",
        "/api/columns/",
    )
    published = [spec.name for spec in CURATED if spec.path.startswith(physical)]

    assert published == []


def test_no_curated_operation_mutates_state() -> None:
    mutating = [
        f"{spec.method} {spec.path}"
        for spec in CURATED
        if spec.method.upper() in _WRITE_METHODS and spec.path not in _READ_ONLY_POSTS
    ]

    assert mutating == []


def test_tool_names_are_unique() -> None:
    names = [spec.name for spec in CURATED]

    assert len(names) == len(set(names))


def test_tool_names_are_plain_identifiers() -> None:
    # Hosts vary in what they accept and some namespace tools by concatenation,
    # so stay well inside the safe set rather than at the edge of the spec.
    bad = [
        spec.name for spec in CURATED if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*", spec.name)
    ]

    assert bad == []


def test_descriptions_do_not_leak_frontend_client_names() -> None:
    # The spec's own text reads "termsApi.list — ..." because it documents the
    # route for whoever maintains the caller. That is noise to an agent, and
    # its presence here would mean an override silently stopped applying.
    leaked = [spec.name for spec in CURATED if "Api." in spec.description]

    assert leaked == []


def test_route_maps_end_with_a_catch_all_exclude() -> None:
    # Without this the allow-list is not one: every uncurated endpoint in the
    # spec would be published too.
    maps = route_maps()

    assert maps[-1].mcp_type.name == "EXCLUDE"
    assert maps[-1].pattern == ".*"
    assert len(maps) == len(CURATED) + 1


def test_collection_pattern_does_not_match_its_item_route() -> None:
    # '/api/terms' unanchored also matches '/api/terms/{term_id}', which would
    # give both routes the same tool identity.
    collection = next(m for m in route_maps() if m.pattern.endswith(r"terms$"))

    assert re.match(collection.pattern, "/api/terms")
    assert not re.match(collection.pattern, "/api/terms/{term_id}")


def test_operation_ids_map_to_curated_names() -> None:
    names = names_by_operation_id(SPEC)

    assert sorted(names.values()) == sorted(spec.name for spec in CURATED)


def test_operation_ids_are_read_from_the_spec_not_guessed() -> None:
    names = names_by_operation_id(SPEC)

    # Confirms the lookup is keyed on the spec's real ids; these are the
    # generated shapes the overrides exist to hide.
    assert names["get_api_terms"] == "search_terms"
    assert names["get_api_terms_term_id_"] == "get_term"


def test_apply_description_overrides_the_generated_text() -> None:
    component = SimpleNamespace(description="termsApi.list — one page of Terms.")

    apply_description(SimpleNamespace(method="GET", path="/api/terms"), component)

    assert component.description.startswith("Search the business glossary")


def test_apply_description_leaves_uncurated_routes_alone() -> None:
    component = SimpleNamespace(description="original")

    apply_description(SimpleNamespace(method="GET", path="/api/not-curated"), component)

    assert component.description == "original"

"""Settings reject an unusable environment at startup, not on first request."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from pytest import MonkeyPatch

from auto_ontology_mcp.config import (
    DEFAULT_CHAT_TIMEOUT_S,
    DEFAULT_PORT,
    DEFAULT_SPEC_PATH,
    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S,
    ConfigError,
    Settings,
    load_settings,
)

_VARS = (
    "AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_URL",
    "AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_TOKEN",
    "AUTO_ONTOLOGY_OPENAPI_SPEC",
    "AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_HOST",
    "AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_PORT",
    "AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_TIMEOUT_S",
    "AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_CHAT_TIMEOUT_S",
    "AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_PUBLIC_URL",
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clean_env(monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """Ignore whatever the developer happens to have exported."""
    for name in _VARS:
        monkeypatch.delenv(name, raising=False)


def test_starts_with_nothing_configured() -> None:
    # Every caller signs in for themselves, so there is no credential to supply
    # and a bare `auto-ontology-mcp` against a local Auto Ontology is a complete configuration.
    settings = load_settings()

    assert settings.api_url == "http://localhost:3000"
    assert settings.port == DEFAULT_PORT
    assert settings.timeout_s == DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S
    assert settings.chat_timeout_s == DEFAULT_CHAT_TIMEOUT_S
    assert settings.spec_path == DEFAULT_SPEC_PATH


def test_holds_no_credential_of_its_own() -> None:
    # Guards the invariant rather than any one variable: a field for a
    # process-wide token is what would let one identity speak for everybody.
    assert not hasattr(load_settings(), "api_token")
    assert "token" not in " ".join(Settings.__dataclass_fields__)


def test_an_exported_api_token_is_ignored(monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    # Anyone who used an earlier build may still have this exported. It must
    # neither be adopted as an identity nor refused at startup.
    monkeypatch.setenv("AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_TOKEN", "auto_ontology_abc")

    assert load_settings().api_url == "http://localhost:3000"


def test_strips_trailing_slash_from_api_url(monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    # httpx joins base_url with a leading-slash path, so a trailing slash here
    # would produce '//api/...' and 404 against the Next.js router.
    monkeypatch.setenv("AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_URL", "https://auto_ontology.example.com/")

    assert load_settings().api_url == "https://auto_ontology.example.com"


def test_rejects_missing_spec(monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch, tmp_path) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("AUTO_ONTOLOGY_OPENAPI_SPEC", str(tmp_path / "nope.json"))

    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="OpenAPI spec not found"):
        load_settings()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["0", "-5", "not-a-number"])
def test_rejects_nonsense_timeouts(monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch, value: str) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_TIMEOUT_S", value)

    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_TIMEOUT_S"):
        load_settings()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["0", "70000", "http"])
def test_rejects_invalid_port(monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch, value: str) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_PORT", value)

    with pytest.raises(ConfigError, match="AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_PORT"):
        load_settings()


def test_blank_values_fall_back_to_defaults(monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    # Unset and empty-string are the same thing to a shell export, so an empty
    # value must not be read as "0" or as a literal blank URL.
    monkeypatch.setenv("AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_PORT", "")
    monkeypatch.setenv("AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_TIMEOUT_S", "  ")

    settings = load_settings()

    assert settings.port == DEFAULT_PORT
    assert settings.timeout_s == DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S


def test_public_url_is_derived_when_unset(monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    # 0.0.0.0 is the default bind address and no use to a browser.
    monkeypatch.setenv("AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_PORT", "9999")

    assert load_settings().public_url == "http://localhost:9999"


def test_public_url_follows_an_explicit_host(monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_HOST", "127.0.0.1")
    monkeypatch.setenv("AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_PORT", "3003")

    # Clients compare this against the address they dialled, and '127.0.0.1' is
    # not the string 'localhost' even though it is the same interface.
    assert load_settings().public_url == "http://127.0.0.1:3003"


def test_public_url_can_be_set_explicitly(monkeypatch: MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("AUTO_ONTOLOGY_MCP_PUBLIC_URL", "https://mcp.example/")

    assert load_settings().public_url == "https://mcp.example"
